title: Geometry - Lesson 1 Practice: Foundations and Notation
description: Practice identifying points, lines, planes, rays, segments, angles, and their notation.

questions.question: Which list contains the three undefined terms in geometry?
questions.explanation: Point, line, and plane are the starting ideas of geometry. Rays, segments, and angles are defined using those ideas.

questions.question: Which notation represents a segment with endpoints A and B?
questions.explanation: A bar over two letters names a segment with two endpoints.

questions.question: $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{BA}$ always name the same ray.
questions.explanation: The first letter names the endpoint of a ray. Reversing the letters usually changes the endpoint and direction.

questions.question: In $\angle PQR$, the vertex is point ______.
questions.explanation: The vertex is the middle letter in a three-letter angle name.

questions.question: Which object is the best real-life model of a plane?
options: A single corner of a book
questions.explanation: A flat tabletop can model a plane because a plane is flat, even though a true plane extends forever.

questions.question: A straight figure has one endpoint and an arrow on the other end. What is it?
questions.explanation: A ray has one endpoint and continues forever in one direction.

questions.question: Explain in one or two sentences why a segment can be measured but a line cannot be measured as a whole.
questions.correctAnswer: A segment has two endpoints, so it has a fixed length. A line extends forever in both directions, so it has no total finite length.
questions.explanation: The key distinction is endpoints. A segment has two endpoints; a line extends without end.

questions.question: A student says the vertex of $\angle ABC$ is A because A is written first. Correct the student's mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: The vertex is B because the vertex is the middle letter in a three-letter angle name.
questions.explanation: For angle names with three letters, the middle letter is always the vertex.
